    Pyrifos: Unequal Random-Intercept Replication

    pyrifos-unequal-random-intercept.Rmd

    The vegan::pyrifos experiment repeatedly sampled 12 ditches. This example deliberately keeps different numbers of dates per ditch to show the Phase 11 estimand and its exchangeability restriction. For a transparent two-level example, dose zero is called control and every positive dose is called treated.

    data(pyrifos, package = "vegan")

ditch <- gl(12, 1, length = 132)
dose_by_ditch <- c(0.1, 0, 0, 0.9, 0, 44, 6, 0.1, 44, 0.9, 0, 6)
treatment <- factor(
  ifelse(dose_by_ditch == 0, "control", "treated"),
  levels = c("control", "treated")
)

# Each size (3, 4, 5, or 6 dates) occurs in both treatment groups.
dates_per_ditch <- c(3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6, 6)
occasion <- ave(seq_len(nrow(pyrifos)), ditch, FUN = seq_along)
keep <- occasion <= dates_per_ditch[ditch]

pyrifos_unequal <- pyrifos[keep, ]
pyrifos_env <- data.frame(
  ditch = droplevels(ditch[keep]),
  treatment = treatment[ditch[keep]]
)
table(table(pyrifos_env$ditch),
      tapply(pyrifos_env$treatment, pyrifos_env$ditch, unique))
#>    
#>     1 2
#>   3 1 2
#>   4 1 2
#>   5 1 2
#>   6 1 2

    The Bray–Curtis geometry is averaged within ditches. Every ditch centroid has equal weight in the treatment hypothesis, regardless of its number of dates. Thus the estimand is the mean ditch community, not the mean observation. The residual permutation moves whole ditch-centroid residuals only among ditches with the same number of retained dates.

    pyrifos_design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ treatment + (1 | ditch),
  pyrifos_env,
  vegdist(pyrifos_unequal, method = "bray")
)

pyrifos_fit <- permanova_unequal_random_intercept(
  pyrifos_design,
  permutations = 199,
  seed = 20260719
)
pyrifos_fit
#> Unequal-replication random-intercept PERMANOVA
#> Estimand: equally weighted random-intercept unit centroids 
#> Permutation: intercept-only cluster-centroid Freedman-Lane residual permutation within equal-size strata (algebraically identical to raw centroid permutation) 
#>                       term df         ss         ms pseudo_f p_perm
#>                  treatment  1 0.05544497 0.05544497 1.419671  0.115
#>  Cluster-centroid Residual 10 0.39054803 0.03905480       NA     NA
    with(pyrifos_fit$test, list(
  estimand = estimand,
  denominator = denominator$expression,
  exchangeable_units = exchangeable_units,
  permutation_strata = permutation_strata,
  approximation_status = approximation_status,
  attainable_permutations = attainable_permutations
))
#> $estimand
#> [1] "equally weighted random-intercept unit centroids"
#> 
#> $denominator
#> [1] "MS[cluster-centroid Residual]"
#> 
#> $exchangeable_units
#> [1] "ditch"
#> 
#> $permutation_strata
#> [1] "exact observation count per random-intercept unit"
#> 
#> $approximation_status
#> [1] "Monte Carlo size-stratified whole-cluster residual permutation"
#> 
#> $attainable_permutations
#> [1] 1296

    This engine does not relax the balanced EMS calculation. It changes the analysis scale to unit centroids and makes empirical inference conditional on replication size. If the size strata cannot generate every treatment contrast, the function rejects instead of reporting an untestable global p-value.
